newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae opponents file proxy at SEC.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae opponents file proxy at SEC.

text.p: The Committee to Restore Value at Sallie Mae said Wednesday it filed proxy materials with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for a special shareholder meeting expected to take place this Summer.

The group, which is opposing the management of Student Loan Marketing Association in a plan to reorganize and privatize the company, is composed of eight current Sallie Mae directors who were elected in 1995.
The group unveiled in the filing its proposed business plan, which includes cutting the company's loan acquisition costs in half by the year 2,000.
The group is also proposing that the company, when private, originate student loans, a move that would put the company in direct competition with banks.
The group said it will name its 15 member slate of directors in the near future.

On June 13, Sallie Mae management filed its business plan with the SEC. In that plan, the company projected a minimum compounded annual growth rate in earnings per share of 15 percent over the next five years.
The management's plan includes moving the company into other non-related business including developing computer software.
Sallie Mae is a government-sponsored enterprise which buys student loans from lenders and securitizes them in the capital markets.
The company was mandated by Congress to become a private entity or to liquidate altogether.
